extracted.intended_audience: researchers, policymakers, journalists, and the public tracking and classifying AI-related incidents
extracted.subtask_description: Documenting and classifying AI incidents in a public incident database (AIM) using the project's taxonomy and metadata fields; includes collecting source reports and grouping similar incidents/variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Domain
rubrics_metrics.description: The Domain Taxonomy of AI Risks classifies risks into seven AI risk domains: (1) Discrimination & toxicity, (2) Privacy & security, (3) Misinformation, (4) Malicious actors & misuse, (5) Human-computer interaction, (6) Socioeconomic & environmental harms, and (7) AI system safety, failures & limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incidents are assigned to one of these seven high-level domains (the example incident is classified as 'Misinformation'). Use the domain that best captures the primary harm type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Subdomain
rubrics_metrics.description: A further 23 subdomains create an accessible and understandable classification of hazards and harms associated with AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign incidents to the appropriate subdomain for finer-grained classification (example shown: '3.1. False or misleading information').

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity (cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Which, if any, entity is presented as the main cause of the risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the actor or entity presented as responsible for the incident (e.g., 'Human', the organization or system developer). Use the entity field to identify alleged developers/operators when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing (lifecycle stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The stage in the AI lifecycle at which the risk is presented as occurring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify whether the incident occurred at e.g., development, deployment, or post-deployment (example: 'Post-deployment').

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the risk is presented as occurring as an expected or unexpected outcome from pursuing a goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label incidents by intent (e.g., 'Intentional' or presumably 'Unintentional') based on how the reports describe motivations or objectives behind the behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source collection standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (AIM) automatically collects and classifies AI-related incidents and hazards in real time from reputable news sources worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incident entries should be backed by reporting from reputable news sources; AIM harvests such coverage in real time. Provide citations/links to the external news reports used as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variant grouping rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A "variant" is an AI incident similar to a known case—it has the same causes, harms, and AI system. Instead of listing it separately, we group it under the first reported incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an incident is substantially the same as an existing entry (same causes, harms, and AI system), record it as a variant under the original incident. Unlike other incidents, variants do not need to have been reported outside the AIID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident reports / evidence list
rubrics_metrics.description: Incident Reports: a timeline/listing of external news reports and analyses that covered the incident (many sources are listed for this incident).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a consolidated timeline/list of reports with links and dates to support the incident narrative and to show breadth of coverage; include diverse reputable outlets where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmed parties / affected entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who or what was harmed by the incident (example: 'General public, Readers of Sports Illustrated and Journalistic integrity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List affected groups, stakeholders, or abstract harms (e.g., 'journalistic integrity') to clarify the impact of the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident metadata and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Incident ID, Report Count, Incident Date, Editors and other metadata are recorded for each incident (example fields: Incident ID 616, Report Count 43, Incident Date 2023-11-27, Editors Daniel Atherton).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain structured metadata for tracking, referencing, and filtering incidents; include counts of reports and editorial attribution where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy classification provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applied Taxonomies: MIT — MIT Taxonomy Classifications — Machine-Classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the taxonomy source and whether classification was machine-classified or manually assigned; this signals provenance and confidence in the classification.
